title_en: Shanghai Baoxiang Cold Storage Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Changxiang Cold Storage Logistics Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of validity of company resolution
ruling_gist_en: The employee representative supervisor on the supervisory board of a limited liability company shall have the status of an employee of the company, and the method of selection of the employee representative supervisor shall comply with the procedures for democratic election by employees as stipulated in Article 51 of the Company Law, and shall meet the representation ratio specified in that Article. If the shareholders' meeting of the company adopts a resolution to appoint an employee representative supervisor, and the appointed supervisor is not an employee of the company, or if the procedure for selecting the appointed supervisor or the representation ratio violates the provisions of Article 51 of the Company Law, such part of the resolution shall be void.

full_text_en:
Shanghai Baoxiang Cold Storage Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Changxiang Cold Storage Logistics Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of validity of company resolution

Ruling Summary

An employee representative supervisor on the board of supervisors of a limited liability company must have the status of an employee of that company. The method of selecting the employee representative supervisor shall comply with the procedure of democratic election by employees as prescribed in Article 51 of the Company Law, and shall also comply with the representation ratio prescribed in that Article. If a shareholders' resolution appoints an employee representative supervisor, and the appointed supervisor is not an employee of the company, or the procedure for the appointment or the representation ratio violates Article 51 of the Company Law, the relevant part of the resolution shall be void.

Plaintiff: Shanghai Baoxiang Cold Storage Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hulin Road, Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Legal representative: Weng Lingsui, executive director of the company.

Defendant: Shanghai Changxiang Cold Storage Logistics Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hulin Road, Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Legal representative: Weng Lingsui, chairperson of the board of directors of the company.

Third Party: Shanghai Jiangyang Aquatic Products Wholesale Trading Market Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at Taihe Road, Baoshan District, Shanghai.

Legal representative: Xu Genfu, executive director of the company.

Third Party: Wei Renli, male, 67 years old, residing at Wanping South Road, Xuhui District, Shanghai.

Third Party: Wei Manhong, male, 64 years old, residing at Gumei Road, Minhang District, Shanghai.

Third Party: Xu Genfu, male, 54 years old, residing at Dongchang Xincun, Pudong New Area, Shanghai.

Third Party: Kong Lingzhi, male, 57 years old, residing at Rende Road, Yangpu District, Shanghai.

Plaintiff Shanghai Baoxiang Cold Storage Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Baoxiang Company) filed an action with the Baoshan District People's Court of Shanghai against Defendant Shanghai Changxiang Cold Storage Logistics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changxiang Company) regarding a dispute over confirmation of the validity of a company resolution.

Plaintiff Baoxiang Company alleged: In January 2014, by acquiring part of the equity of Defendant Changxiang Company from Third Party Shanghai Jiangyang Aquatic Products Wholesale Trading Market Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiangyang Company), Plaintiff became a shareholder of Defendant Changxiang Company, with Plaintiff and Third Party each holding 50% of the equity in Changxiang Company. In April 2014, Changxiang Company convened an interim shareholders' meeting and adopted a shareholders' resolution (i.e., the disputed shareholders' resolution). Item 2 of that shareholders' resolution resolved to establish a board of supervisors, appointing Xu Genfu and Kong Lingzhi as shareholder representative supervisors, appointing Wei Renli as the employee representative supervisor, and removing Wei Manhong from the position of supervisor. Before Plaintiff acquired equity in Changxiang Company, Plaintiff was not familiar with the composition of personnel of Jiangyang Company and Changxiang Company. Later, Plaintiff discovered that Wei Renli was the legal representative of Jiangyang Company, was not an employee of Changxiang Company, and was not qualified to serve as the employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company. Plaintiff believed that the content regarding the appointment and removal of supervisors and the voting procedure in the disputed shareholders' resolution both violated the relevant provisions of the Company Law concerning employee representative supervisors, and that Wei Renli could not serve as the employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company. Therefore, Plaintiff requested the court to enter a judgment: declaring that the clause of the shareholders' resolution adopted by Defendant Changxiang Company in April 2014 concerning the composition of the company's board of supervisors was void.

Defendant Changxiang Company argued: The resolution to elect Wei Renli as the employee representative supervisor was formed through a lawful procedure and had been filed with the administrative department for industry and commerce. Therefore, Defendant requested the court to dismiss the claims of Plaintiff Baoxiang Company.

Third Party Jiangyang Company, Third Party Wei Renli, and Third Party Xu Genfu jointly submitted statements: Wei Renli had served as the legal representative of Changxiang Company for a long period and only stepped down in 2013, but he was still responsible for some affairs of Changxiang Company. Wei Renli was elected in April 2014 as the employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company through a procedure of election, and this was confirmed by the disputed shareholders' resolution. After retirement, Wei Renli was re-employed by Changxiang Company under a re-employment arrangement, and there was still an employment relationship between him and Changxiang Company, which satisfied the statutory requirements concerning the status of an employee supervisor under the Company Law. Therefore, the disputed shareholders' resolution was valid, and they requested the court to dismiss the claims of Plaintiff Baoxiang Company.

Third Party Wei Manhong stated: He accepted the removal of his supervisory position by the disputed shareholders' resolution.

Third Party Kong Lingzhi stated: He was appointed by Plaintiff Baoxiang Company to serve as a supervisor at Changxiang Company. The grounds asserted by Plaintiff were valid, and Wei Renli was not qualified to serve as the employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company.

After trial at first instance, the Baoshan District People's Court of Shanghai found the following facts:

Defendant Changxiang Company was originally a wholly-owned subsidiary of Third Party Jiangyang Company. In January 2014, Plaintiff Baoxiang Company and Jiangyang Company entered into an equity transfer agreement, stipulating that Jiangyang Company would transfer 50% of the equity in Changxiang Company to Plaintiff, and thereafter Plaintiff and Jiangyang Company each held 50% of the equity in Changxiang Company. Subsequently, the parties completed the procedures for registration of equity change. In April 2014, Changxiang Company convened an interim shareholders' meeting and adopted the disputed shareholders' resolution. Item 2 of the resolution provided: establishing a board of supervisors of the company; appointing Xu Genfu and Kong Lingzhi as shareholder representative supervisors; removing Wei Manhong from the position of supervisor; and appointing Wei Renli as the other employee representative supervisor. The resolution also made appointments and removals regarding directors and amended the company's articles of association.

Wei Renli was born in 1948 and had reached the statutory retirement age in 2008. He served as the legal representative of Defendant Changxiang Company until stepping down in 2013. At the time of the litigation, he was still the legal representative of Third Party Jiangyang Company, but stepped down during the litigation. There was no evidence showing that there was a labor relationship between Wei Renli and Changxiang Company since April 2014.

Among the materials filed with the administrative department for industry and commerce for the registration of Defendant Changxiang Company, there was a resolution of the employees' congress of Changxiang Company dated April 30, 2014. The main content was: The employees' congress of Changxiang Company was held on April 30, 2014; five employee representatives were required to attend, and five were actually present; the meeting was presided over by Wei Renli; the meeting elected Wei Renli as the employee supervisor of the company; five persons voted in favor, representing 100% of the total employee representatives; in the signature section of the attending employees, there was no signature of Wei Renli, and the five persons who signed as "employee representatives" were "Zhu", "Fan", "Yang", "Ling", and "Zhang". However, social insurance premiums for these five "employee representatives" were not paid by Changxiang Company after May 2014. Upon examination of other evidentiary materials, only the evidence regarding the establishment of labor relationships between Fan, Zhang, and Changxiang Company was relatively sufficient; it was difficult to prove that the other three persons had labor relationships with Changxiang Company. Moreover, there was a lack of evidence proving that these five persons had been elected as employee representatives by all employees of Changxiang Company or could represent the will of all employees of Changxiang Company.

The court of first instance, the Baoshan District People's Court of Shanghai, held:

Pursuant to Article 51 of the Company Law of the PRC, where a limited liability company establishes a board of supervisors, the proportion of employee representatives on the board of supervisors shall not be less than one-third; and the employee representatives on the board of supervisors shall be democratically elected by the employees of the company through the employees' congress, the general meeting of employees, or other forms. This provision is established to ensure that the company does not infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of employees in the course of business decision-making and management, and to safeguard the democratic rights of employees in modern corporate governance; it is mandatory and must be complied with when a company establishes a board of supervisors. According to this provision, first, an employee representative supervisor must be elected from among the employees of the company; a person who does not have a labor relationship with the company cannot become an employee representative supervisor. Second, an employee representative supervisor must be democratically elected by the employees of the company through the employees' congress, the general meeting of employees, or other forms; if a person who does not have the status of an employee or a person who has not been elected through democratic procedures by employees is appointed as an employee representative supervisor, such appointment shall be void.

In this case, Wei Renli, the employee representative supervisor appointed by the disputed shareholders' resolution, did not have a labor relationship with Defendant Changxiang Company at the time of his appointment or thereafter, and he did not have the status of an employee of Changxiang Company. Moreover, Wei Renli had previously served for a long period as the legal representative of Changxiang Company and as the legal representative of Jiangyang Company, the controlling shareholder of Changxiang Company; such positions represented the status and will of the senior management of Changxiang Company and could not represent the status and will of the employees of Changxiang Company. Therefore, Wei Renli did not have the qualification to serve as an employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company. Additionally, based on the evidence on record, among the five persons — "Zhu", "Fan", "Yang", "Ling", and "Zhang" — who elected Wei Renli as the employee representative supervisor, only two, Fan and Zhang, had labor relationships with Changxiang Company; it was difficult to prove that the other three had labor relationships with Changxiang Company, and it was difficult to prove that these five persons had been elected as employee representatives by all employees of Changxiang Company or could represent the will of all employees of Changxiang Company. Therefore, the procedure for appointing Wei Renli as the employee representative supervisor also did not comply with the provisions of the Company Law. In summary, the clause in the disputed shareholders' resolution appointing Wei Renli as the employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company should be void. Since the board of supervisors functions as a whole, the clause in that resolution regarding the composition of the board of supervisors should also be void. Changxiang Company should re-elect and select eligible members for the board of supervisors in accordance with the Company Law and the company's articles of association.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 22, Paragraph 1 and Article 51 of the Company Law of the PRC, the Baoshan District People's Court of Shanghai rendered judgment on December 1, 2016:

Item 2 of the shareholders' resolution adopted by Defendant Shanghai Changxiang Cold Storage Logistics Co., Ltd. on April 30, 2014 (i.e., establishing a board of supervisors of the company, appointing Xu Genfu and Kong Lingzhi as shareholder representative supervisors, removing Wei Manhong from the position of supervisor, and appointing Wei Renli as the other employee supervisor) is void.

Jiangyang Company and Wei Renli, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, arguing: The procedure of the disputed shareholders' resolution was lawful, and its content was true and valid, having been confirmed by the shareholders and registered with the administrative department for industry and commerce. The procedure for electing Wei Renli as the employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company, the defendant at first instance, was also lawful and valid; the employees who signed the resolution of the employees' congress were employees of Changxiang Company at that time and all had voting qualifications. Wei Renli was qualified to serve as an employee supervisor of Changxiang Company; "employee" under the Company Law is not limited to those in a labor relationship but should include those in a service relationship, part-time workers, etc. The two appellants requested the court of second instance to amend the judgment and dismiss the claims of the appellee Baoxiang Company.

Appellee Baoxiang Company argued: The appellate claims of Appellants Jiangyang Company and Wei Renli had no factual or legal basis and should be rejected. Wei Renli was not an employee of Changxiang Company, had never received a salary from Changxiang Company, and did not have the qualification to serve as an employee representative. Moreover, the majority of the employees who signed the so-called resolution of the employees' congress in the materials for industrial and commercial registration were not employees of Changxiang Company, and the election procedure was unlawful; therefore, the disputed shareholders' resolution was void. The facts found by the court of first instance were correct and the law was applied accurately. The appellants' grounds of appeal could not stand, and the appellee requested the court of second instance to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The defendant at first instance, Changxiang Company, and Third Party Kong Lingzhi, concurred with the opinions of the appellee Baoxiang Company at the second instance.

The third parties at first instance, Wei Manhong and Xu Genfu, concurred with the opinions of the appellants Jiangyang Company and Wei Renli at the second instance.

Upon second instance, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The court of second instance, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, held: Entering into a labor contract or having a de facto labor relationship with the company is a necessary condition for becoming an employee representative supervisor. Appellant Wei Renli did not have the qualification to serve as an employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company, the defendant at first instance, for the following reasons. First, the employees' congress is an important system for coordinating labor relations, and an employee representative must have a labor relationship with the company. Reference is made to Article 23 of the "Regulations on Democratic Management of Enterprises" formulated by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC), the All-China Federation of Trade Unions, and other departments: "Employees who have signed a labor contract with the enterprise, establishing a labor relationship, or employees who have a de facto labor relationship with the enterprise, have the right to elect and be elected as representatives to the employees' congress. The representative qualification of an employee representative whose labor relationship is lawfully terminated or dissolved shall be automatically terminated." In this case, when the disputed shareholders' resolution was adopted, Wei Renli no longer held a position at Changxiang Company, did not receive a salary from Changxiang Company, i.e., there was no labor relationship between him and Changxiang Company; therefore, Wei Renli did not have the qualification to serve as an employee representative. Second, an employee representative supervisor should be democratically elected from among the employee representatives through the employees' congress, the general meeting of employees, or other forms. Article 51, Paragraph 2 of the Company Law provides that the board of supervisors shall include employee representatives of the company, indicating that the qualification of an employee representative is a prerequisite for becoming an employee representative supervisor. In this case, Wei Renli was not an employee representative; therefore, he did not have the qualification to serve as an employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company. Moreover, Article 51, Paragraph 2 of the Company Law also provides that the proportion of employee representatives on the board of supervisors shall not be less than one-third. This proportion is a mandatory provision of the Company Law concerning validity. In this case, Wei Renli did not have employee representative qualifications, and the other two supervisors were shareholder representatives, resulting in a zero proportion of employee representatives, which violated the aforementioned provision. Therefore, the court of first instance correctly held that the clause in the disputed shareholders' resolution appointing Wei Renli as the employee representative supervisor of Changxiang Company was void, and the court of second instance affirmed this. As for the appellants' contention that the procedure for electing the employee representative supervisor was lawful and that the signing employees all had voting qualifications, since Wei Renli did not have employee representative qualifications, regardless of whether the signing employees had voting qualifications, this could not change the fact that there was no employee representative on the board of supervisors, nor could it cure the validity of the relevant clauses of the disputed shareholders' resolution. Therefore, the court of second instance did not accept this contention of the appellants.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment on March 10, 2017:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment. This judgment is final.
